media._mediaNote:
THE 65.374s BED IS SHORTER THAN THIS FILM AND THE KIT DOES NOT LOOP IT. `build` sizes the bgm slot to the film's length; the media itself just runs out, so the last eleven seconds of a 76-second cut — `what-stays-yours` and the whole sign-off — would have played dry, with no error and no warning.

`ci-campaign-bed-110.mp3` is the same bed crossfaded into itself and cut at 110s. The join uses `c1=qsin:c2=qsin`, NOT the `tri` the house recipe suggests, and the difference is measurable rather than cosmetic: the source track fades itself out over its last ~1.4s (t=64s reads -43.1 dB against a -18.5 dB body), so a 5s crossfade at 60.4s is mixing a fade-out into a fade-in. Under `tri` the join dipped to -22.4 dB, about 4 dB under the bed's own level; under equal-power `qsin` the worst point is -19.6 dB, within 1 dB of the body. Sampled every 2s across 55-72s.

Integrated loudness is -16.8 LUFS against the source's -16.6, so `musicGain` computes the same trim it always did. 110s leaves headroom for a longer re-cut; the kit fades the bed out over 1.6s at the end of the film regardless of how much bed is left.

scenes.title: A year of conversations.
scenes.caption: You have never once looked at it.
scenes.narration: You have been talking to this thing for a year. You have never once looked at it, because there has never been anything to look at.
scenes._editNote:
The pain, stated as the user actually experiences it. Typographic rather than a screen: the subject of this beat is an ABSENCE, and the only way to shoot an absence is to caption a blank — which is what this card is.

The three em-dashes are the beat, and they set up the title card two scenes later ('A face and a body, in a browser tab.') by naming what is missing first.

They are also load-bearing for the frozen-picture gate. A `feature` with a title and NO items paints once and then holds: both the paced reveal and the drift target the chips row (`.<id>-chips`), so an itemless card has literally nothing in motion for its whole length. Measured on the Companion Scan film in this same rewrite: three itemless cards took that cut to 11% landscape / 14% portrait against an 8% bar, and adding items took it to 0%/0%. Do not strip these back out.

scenes.title: Most people quit right about here.
scenes.caption: The usual price of a face.
scenes.narration: Giving an assistant a face usually means a game engine, a character rig, and a bill that runs by the minute. Most people quit right about here.

scenes.title: Spatial Companion
scenes.caption: A face, a voice and a body — in a browser tab.
scenes.narration: This one is a browser tab.
scenes._editNote:
The voice is back on the title card, and it is now earned. This scene deliberately dropped the word while a stock install was mute; #157 landed on main and made `browser` (speechSynthesis) the DEFAULT TTS mode, so a clean checkout speaks with nothing installed. The card claims a face, a voice and a body, and the product now has all three out of the box.

The rule that put it in the recap in the first place still stands for anything else: a title card is the worst place in a film for a claim the pictures cannot back. This one is carried by the product, not by the frame, and that is only acceptable because it is now true of every install rather than of a configured one.

scenes.caption: It asks once. Skip goes straight to text.
scenes.narration: It asks for a microphone once, on the first load. Skip it, and type instead.

shots.alt: First-run onboarding modal asking for microphone access, over the blurred avatar scene, with a Skip option
shots._pointerNote:
The caption is "Skip goes straight to text" and Skip is the one control on screen the film ever asks anyone to press, so this is the shot that has to show it being pressed rather than described.

Both points are the centre of the Skip button, read off the committed plate rather than computed: on the 3840x2160 landscape plate the button box is centred at (1958, 1231) px = (0.510, 0.570); on the 1080x1920 phone plate at (581, 1110) px = (0.538, 0.578). They differ because the modal is a fixed-width card centred in a 1280px page and a near-full-width card in a 360px one, so the button pair sits at a different fraction of the image in each cut — this is exactly the case the per-format form exists for.

Portrait renders as a tap, not a cursor, and that is not a choice made here: `pointerStyle` reads the DEVICE FRAME, and the portrait cut's default frame is the phone. A mouse arrow gliding across a phone screen would be a lie about how this is used.

scenes.caption: Nothing in the log yet. It is already looking at you.
scenes.narration: Past the modal there is no account, no sign-in and nothing in the log. There is just something on the other side of it, already awake.
scenes._editNote: This is the film's presence beat and the reason the pain card works. The chat panel's own empty state does the arguing — 'Nothing here yet. Say hello, or type below — the whole conversation stays on this machine.' — so the caption does not have to repeat it.

shots.alt: The HUD around a live avatar: the Companion Intelligence logo card, an empty chat log promising the conversation stays on this machine, a message input and the control dock
shots._portraitRefitNote:
THE PORTRAIT RECTANGLE WAS RE-DERIVED ON 2026-08-13, AND THE NOTE BELOW IS WHY IT HAD TO BE.

That note reasons from `1.290323 / w` in landscape and a 0.738 floor in portrait, and both are now half the calculation. The kit's focus geometry gained a HEIGHT coefficient — landscape `min(1.290323/w, 1.145758/h)`, portrait `min(1.398964/w, 1.227306/h)` — and height binds sooner than width, by about 13%. A square rectangle therefore no longer lands the window the note computed: `0.738 x 0.738` asks for 1.663, not 1.895, and yields a 0.838 window rather than 0.738.

The consequence here was exactly the defect the note says it backed out of. A 0.838 window cannot start at y 0.235 — 0.235 + 0.838 > 1 — so it slid up to 0.162, back inside the empty-log panel, and `ci-video focus-preview` shows the end frame slicing the log's own paragraph at both edges: "othing here yet. Say hello, or type below — the whole / onversation stays on this machine." The note's whole point was that no window under 1.0 can contain that panel, so it must be cleared instead.

0.67 square at (0.13, 0.2805) asks for 1.832 and gets it, for a 0.760 window. 0.760 is the largest window whose top can sit below the log panel's bottom edge (0.228) without the bottom running off the plate: it lands at y 0.239, clearing the panel by 0.011, and the window centre stays on the head centre (0.465). Reconstructed and looked at — a clean bust, the message input legible, the control dock's top row above the caption band, and no fragment of the log.

The landscape rectangle is unchanged. It now yields 0.606 rather than the 0.538 the note claims, which is looser than intended but frames the same clean bust with the chat rail outside it; verified in the same pass.
shots._focusNote:
THE PRESENCE BEAT, AND IT HAD NO SUBJECT. This shot declared `push-in` with no `focus`, which is the kit's 1.045 linear creep — 0.75%/second, under the threshold of noticing. The scene whose whole argument is "it is already looking at you" was a full-page screenshot being held.

The narration lands in this order: no account, no sign-in, nothing in the log — and then the presence. So the move starts wide, where the empty Chat Log rail is legible and does the arguing, and ends on the face. That is the shot-size change, and it also puts the punchline where the last frame is.

Landscape 0.538 square at (0.231, 0.151). 0.538 is the FLOOR — 1.290323/0.538 = 2.398, a hair under MAX_SCALE, so the rectangle is still read and the window is 53.8% of the plate, the tightest 16:9 framing the grammar allows. Centred on the head (0.5, 0.42), measured off the plate: hair crown y 0.271, chin y 0.556, temples x 0.441..0.559. Reconstructed end frame checked: a clean bust, nothing sliced, and the chat rail (x 0.823..1.0) falls outside the window rather than being cut through.

PORTRAIT IS NOT THE SAME RECTANGLE, and the reason is a defect I hit and backed out of. The obvious mirror — the 0.738 window centred on the face — starts at y 0.031 and slices the empty-log paragraph through the middle of its glyphs at BOTH edges: "...hing here yet" / "...ersation stays on this machine." The log is full-bleed at 360px, so no window under 1.0 can contain it. Dropped to y 0.235, just below the log panel's bottom edge (0.228), so the log leaves frame cleanly instead of being cut in half. x stays 0.096 to put the window centre on the head centre (0.465). The control dock then sits in the lower third, and the collapse chevron in the bottom-left corner is clipped — it is at y 0.955, under the caption scrim, and is the only thing given up.

scenes.caption: One turn: lip sync, expression, a body clip.
scenes.narration: Type a message. The reply lands in the log, and the same reply drives the mouth, the face and a body clip.

shots.alt: A question typed into the chat input, ready to send
shots._pointerNote:
THE SEND BUTTON, AND THIS IS THE SHOT THE WHOLE CURSOR IDEA IS FOR. The two shots of this scene are the same screen a beat apart — a question sitting in the input, then the question and its reply in the log. What happens between them is a click, and until now the film simply dissolved over it and hoped the caption carried it. A cursor that arrives on the send button and presses it is the only thing in this storyboard that shows the product being USED rather than photographed.

Centre of the circular send control, measured on the plates: landscape (2342, 1799) px of 3840x2160 = (0.610, 0.833); portrait (839, 1434) px of 1080x1920 = (0.777, 0.747). Both were checked by drawing the point back onto the plate, not derived from the layout.

A POINTER HERE IS SAFE WHERE A FOCUS WOULD NOT BE. This is shot 1 of 2 and layer 0 crossfades out partway through the scene's single camera tween, so a focus declared here would never be reached. `pointerPlan` is given the LAYER's window rather than the scene's, so the click is placed inside the span this shot is actually the visible one — which is why the cursor goes here and the focus goes on `chat-turn`.

No `at`. The default is 58% of that layer's window, which is past the caption's arrival and clear of the outgoing dissolve; a hand-set time would be measured against a scene length that `pacing: "fit"` re-derives from the narration on every render.

shots.alt: The same HUD after sending: the question and the avatar’s reply are both in the chat log
shots._focusNote:
LANDSCAPE ONLY, DELIBERATELY — see the second half of this note.

Motion changed from `drift-down` to `push-in` because the shot now has a subject and the subject is at the TOP of the plate. With a focus, `drift-down` starts on the subject and travels down THROUGH it; on a chat log that is a move away from the thing that just appeared. `push-in` ends on it.

0.72 square at (0.28, 0) — window x 0.28..1.0, y 0..0.72, scale 1.792. It is deliberately LOOSER than the 0.538 floor, and asking for less is the whole point: this repo already owns the defect where a rectangle aimed at the chat rail produced a frame with half a face sliced off in the corner (it is cited by name in the kit's own camera.mjs). The rail is 0.177 wide and no legal window is narrower than 0.538, so a rectangle aimed at the rail alone cannot avoid catching part of the head. At 0.72 the head (x 0.441..0.559) is INSIDE the window whole, and the end frame is a two-shot: the face on the left third, the question and the reply legible on the right. Reconstructed and looked at — both bubbles, both avatar chips and the "Chat Log" heading are complete, nothing clipped.

WHY NO PORTRAIT RECTANGLE. At 360px the log is a full-width panel across the top, and the two rows together span x 0.036..0.955 of the plate — 0.919 wide. The tightest portrait window is 0.738. There is therefore NO placement of any legal rectangle that does not cut a bubble edge or an avatar chip: the version I checked rendered "Chat Log" as "Log" and sliced the assistant bubble's left edge through the text. A format left out keeps the plain move, which is the correct outcome here — a missing focus is a wide shot, a wrong one is a frame that reads as broken.

scenes.caption: Collapse the dock. A face and one line.
scenes.narration: Hide the panels and what is left is a face and one line to type into.

shots.alt: The same scene with the control dock and chat panel collapsed, leaving the avatar and a single message input
shots._focusNote:
THE ONLY REVEAL IN THE FILM, AND THE BEAT IS A REVEAL. "Hide the panels and what is left is a face and one line to type into" is a sentence about what is ABSENT, and you cannot photograph an absence by pushing into it. `pull-back` starts on the focus and ends at rest, so the shot opens tight on the face and opens out to the bare screen with the two collapsed pills and a single input line — the emptiness arrives as the move, which is what the line claims.

It is also the counterweight to `already-there`. That scene pushes IN to this same face from the same wide; this one starts there and leaves. Same rectangle at 16:9 on purpose — the two scenes are the same framing run in opposite directions, which is a rhythm change the cut did not have when both were `push-in`.

Landscape reuses the 0.538 floor square at (0.231, 0.151); the collapsed "Chat" pill (0.962, 0.031) and "Controls" pill (0.045, 0.960) both fall outside it, so the opening frame is the face alone and the pills are part of what the pull-back reveals.

Portrait is (0.096, 0.105), NOT the 0.031 the landscape maps to. At 0.031 the window's top edge lands inside the header bar and cuts the logo card and the "Chat" pill in half — a sliced pill in the first frame of the shot reads as a broken render. 0.105 clears the header divider (0.097). The window then runs 0.105..0.843, which holds the face and the message input complete and leaves the Controls pill (y 0.955) to the reveal. Reconstructed and checked at both formats.

scenes._transitionNote:
The only transition added in this pass, and the only boundary in the film where a cut is both safe and needed.

NEEDED: `quiet` and this scene are the SAME app screen a beat apart — the settings dialog simply opens over the avatar the previous shot ended on. A cross-dissolve between two shots of one screen reads as a double-exposure ghost, with the dialog fading up through the face. It is also the meet -> wire chapter change, and the film had no punctuation there at all.

SAFE: a cut suppresses the incoming dissolve, which is what was covering the previous scene's tail — so before adding one you have to know what the previous scene IS. Here it is `quiet`, a `screen` scene, and after this pass it is a pull-back: its tail is a moving picture, not a static card holding after its narration has stopped. The two boundaries where that is NOT true — `title` (after the `quit` card) and `first-run` (after the `title` card) — are deliberately left dissolving for exactly this reason.
scenes.caption: Your model, your endpoint.
scenes.narration: Point it at your own Ollama, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you run, or a proxy of your choosing.

shots.alt: The settings panel with Ollama selected as the model provider and a local endpoint filled in
shots._pointerNote:
The Server URL field, because the caption's second half is "your endpoint" and this is the field that makes it true — the row that exists for `ollama` and does not exist for `mlc`, which is the visible difference between this dialog and `in-the-tab`'s.

The provider select is one row above and is the pointer target on `in-the-tab` instead. Deliberately split: two consecutive scenes of the same dialog clicking the same control would be the cursor decorating the shot rather than using it. Here the beat is where you point it; there the beat is picking what runs it.

Centre of the input box, read off the plates: landscape (1916, 754) px of 3840x2160 = (0.499, 0.349); portrait (536, 634) px of 1080x1920 = (0.496, 0.330). Marked back onto both plates and checked to land inside the box, vertically centred.

BOTH POINTS SURVIVE THIS SHOT'S CAMERA MOVE. The push ends on a window of x 0.131..0.669 / y 0..0.538 at 16:9 and x 0.031..0.769 / y 0..0.738 at 9:16; the hotspot is inside both, so the cursor is on canvas from the start of the push to the end of it rather than being carried off the edge before it can press.
shots._portraitRefitNote:
RE-DERIVED 2026-08-13 BECAUSE THE 9:16 FRAME WAS SLICING THE DIALOG DOWN ITS RIGHT EDGE.

Same root cause as the one written up on `hud-shell`: the kit's focus scale now takes the min of a width and a HEIGHT coefficient, so `0.738 x 0.738` no longer buys the 0.738 window this rectangle was drawn against — it buys 0.838. A 0.838 window centred on the rectangle's centre (x 0.4) runs -0.019..0.819, clamps to the left edge at 0.002..0.840, and the Ollama dialog's content spans x 0.126..0.874 of the phone plate. Everything past 0.840 was cut off at the canvas edge: the provider select's chevron and both Behavior toggles, sliced vertically. A control cut in half at the frame edge reads as a broken render, and neither `check` nor the layout gate has anything to say about it.

0.722 square at (0.139, 0.093) gives a 0.820 window at x 0.09..0.91 and y 0.093..0.913, which contains the whole dialog with margin on both sides. The y is 0.049 lower than centring implies because the window is offset down the plate by half the caption allowance; without that correction the "Settings" header sat above the frame. Reconstructed with `ci-video focus-preview` and looked at: header complete, `http://localhost:11434` and `gemma3:1b` legible in the upper half, every toggle whole, the caption band over the GRAPHICS row.

The pointer at (0.496, 0.330) is well inside the new window; `check` re-resolves all eight pointers and passes.

LANDSCAPE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. It yields a 0.606 window rather than the 0.538 the note below computes, so the dialog sits smaller and right of centre with dead space to its left. That is weaker composition, not a defect — nothing is cut — and re-centring every landscape rectangle in the fleet is a separate pass against the kit change, not something to do in one repo.
shots._focusNote:
A LOOSER RECT THAN `settings-on-device`, AND IT HAS TO BE LOOSER.

These two scenes are the same dialog a beat apart, and only the second had a focus — so the pair cut from a wide frame, where the panel sits in the middle third of a 3840px plate, straight to a close-up of the same panel. Matching them was the point of adding this.

The obvious move — copy `settings-on-device`'s 0.6 square at (0.2, 0.045) — is WRONG here, and the focus-preview shows why in one frame: it slices the word 'Settings' in half along the top edge. The dialog is vertically centred, and the Ollama panel carries a Server URL field that the WebLLM panel does not, so it is taller and its header sits HIGHER in the plate. The same rectangle lands below it.

0.36 x 0.45 at (0.32, 0.02) instead. That asks for 2.22x and gets 2.4x — CLAMPED by MAX_SCALE, so the window lands at 53.8% of the plate rather than the 45% requested, i.e. slightly looser than asked. Checked rather than assumed, and the looser framing is the better one: the dialog's rounded top corner stays in shot, so it reads as a panel rather than as a slice. It frames the dialog top through the Model field — the provider, the endpoint and the model name, which is the whole claim of the beat — and leaves BEHAVIOR, GRAPHICS and the Save/Cancel footer outside. Verified against `ci-video focus-preview`, not computed and trusted.

No re-capture needed: `focus` is a camera move the builder applies to the committed plate, not a capture-time crop.

scenes.caption: On-device: the model runs in the tab.
scenes.narration: Or pick on-device, and one of the five providers runs the model inside the browser tab itself.

shots.alt: The settings panel with On-device (WebLLM) selected as the model provider
shots._pointerNote:
The LLM provider select, because the narration is "pick on-device" and this is the control that picks it. The frame already shows the RESULT of that choice — the capture drives the select to `mlc`, which is why the Server URL row is missing and the dialog is a visibly different shape from `your-model`'s. The cursor supplies the act the still cannot: it lands on the select that produced the state on screen.

Centre of the select box, read off the plates: landscape (1916, 661) px of 3840x2160 = (0.499, 0.306); portrait (536, 540) px of 1080x1920 = (0.496, 0.281). Marked back onto both plates and confirmed inside the control.

Y differs from `your-model`'s pointer by more than the one row you would expect (0.306 vs 0.349 at 16:9) because the two dialogs are not the same height: dropping the Server URL row shortens the panel, and the dialog is vertically centred, so every row above the fold moves DOWN in the plate. That is the same fact `your-model`'s focus note records about slicing the word "Settings" — the two dialogs cannot share coordinates, and a pointer copied from the neighbouring scene would land in the gap above the select.

Both points sit inside this shot's focus window (x 0.131..0.669 / y 0.007..0.545 at 16:9; x 0.031..0.769 / y 0..0.738 at 9:16), so the push carries the cursor with the control it is pressing rather than off the frame.
shots._focusNote: Focused on the CONNECTION block, which is the beat. It also frames out a real defect at 9:16: mlc has one field fewer than ollama, so the dialog's scroll container lands its boundary mid-row and slices 'WebGPU rendering' through the middle of the glyphs. The committed ollama shot happens to cut cleanly at a divider instead. This is the app's own scroll clipping at 360x640, not a capture artefact, and it is not worth masking — but there is no reason to put it on screen.
shots._portraitRefitNote:
RE-DERIVED 2026-08-13, same fault and same cause as `settings-panel` — see the long note there. The 0.738 square now buys a 0.838 window, it clamped to the left edge, and the right side of the dialog was cut off at the canvas: the provider select's chevron and both Behavior toggles.

This dialog is SHORTER than the Ollama one, because `mlc` has no Server URL row, so it takes a tighter rectangle than its neighbour: 0.669 square at (0.1655, 0.12), a 0.760 window at x 0.12..0.88 / y 0.12..0.88. Checked in `focus-preview`: "Settings", CONNECTION, `On-device (WebLLM)` and `Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC` all complete and in the upper half, every toggle whole, Save and Cancel in shot, the caption band over the GRAPHICS row.

WHAT THIS GIVES UP, STATED PLAINLY. The `_focusNote` below kept the GRAPHICS block out of frame because the app's own scroll container clips "WebGPU rendering" at 360x640, and the mlc dialog cuts mid-row where the Ollama one happens to cut at a divider. There is no rectangle that both contains the dialog's width and excludes that row: the content is 0.748 of the plate wide, the portrait window floor is 0.738, and the window is square. Between a control sliced at the canvas edge and the app's own scroll fade, the app's fade is the honest frame — it is what a user at that width sees. The clipping is still the product's, is still worth fixing in the product, and is not masked here.
shots._captureNote: Establishes onboarding ITSELF (the eval below), for the reason written up on datacenter-diorama: shot order is not a declared dependency and `--only` does not replay it. Selecting `mlc` is the point of the frame, not decoration — FIELD_MAP in SettingsPanel.tsx gives mlc a modelKey and NO urlKey, so the Server URL row disappears and the dialog is visibly a different shape from the Ollama one in `connection`. Nothing is typed here: the model shown is the app's own default (llmConfig.ts defaultLLMConfig.mlc_model), which is the honest thing to film.

scenes.caption: One room ships with it: a 1970s research datacenter.
scenes.narration: Put a room around it, and the camera steps back far enough to bring the whole body into frame.
scenes._editNote: The only environment in the product besides the plain studio — EnvironmentPreset is 'none' | 'datacenter-1970s'. Worded as one room for that reason. The two props whose GLBs do not match their filenames are excluded by PROP_NEEDS_REEXPORT and are not in these frames.

shots.alt: The avatar standing full-length in the 1970s research datacenter: a plotter on a desk, a minicomputer with a printer, a tape reel and cabinets behind
shots._motionNote:
`drift-down` -> `pull-back`, to say what the narration says: "the camera steps back far enough to bring the whole body into frame." A drift travelled down into the unlit ceiling that fills the top third of this plate; a pull-back opens out, which is the sentence.

No `focus` is declared here ON PURPOSE, and that is the whole reason this change is safe. This is shot 1 of 2 and the scene has ONE camera tween shared across both layers, so layer 0 dissolves out at roughly the halfway point of the move. A focus declared here would never be reached, and a focus move that is interrupted mid-push leaves the device frame's edge slicing across the canvas. Without one, `pull-back` is the legacy mirror — 1.045 down to rest — so the frame is a card on the ground for every frame it is on screen and being cut away halfway costs nothing. The subject-bearing rectangle stays on `datacenter-quiet`, which is the shot that is still up when the tween ends.
shots._captureNote: Dismisses onboarding ITSELF rather than inheriting it. Every shot after hud-shell used to rely on hud-shell's Skip click having persisted ci_avatar_onboarded into the shared browser context — an ordering dependency nothing declares. It holds for a full run and breaks the moment anyone re-shoots one shot: `make.sh --only datacenter-diorama` captured this frame with the Enable Microphone modal and its blur backdrop over the whole room. The step below is an eval, not a click, because it has to be a no-op on the full run too: by the time this shot runs in order the key is already set, the Skip button does not exist, and a plain click step would fail the run.
shots._poseNote: The wait is 9000, not 3000, and it is about the avatar's ARMS. On load the rig greets (a Waving clip) before it settles into its idle, and the greet is still unwinding at +6s — arms out, fingers spread, which photographs as a mannequin rather than a character. Sampled on Metal at networkidle + N ms: 1000 bind pose, 2500 arms overhead mid-wave, 4000-6000 arms coming down, 10000+ a settled idle with the arms hanging naturally. 9000 + settle 3000 lands well clear of it. See capture.config.mjs hazard 12 for the other half of this — under a software rasteriser the mixer never drives the rig at all and NO settle helps, which is what put the A-pose in the shots this replaced.

shots.alt: The same room with the dock and chat panel collapsed, leaving the avatar full-length in the diorama
shots._focusNote:
push-in, not drift-down, and with a subject. The room only occupies the lower two thirds of the plate — above the machines is unlit ceiling, and it is a third of the 9:16 crop. A drift-down would spend the shot travelling INTO that emptiness. The focus rects instead end the push on the desk-and-avatar band at 16:9 and on the avatar at 9:16, so the move settles on something and the dead air at the top is cropped out rather than approached.

Landscape widened 0.72 -> 0.80 (1.79x -> 1.61x) on 2026-08-07, because the caption of this very scene is "Body included." and the old rectangle cut the avatar at the knee — the shot argued against its own caption. It also slid: at 0.72 the kit reported the window sliding back to y 0.279 from the requested 0.30, and left a fragment of the collapsed Controls button showing under the caption band. At 0.80 the figure reads full-length from head to shin, the far-right machine pair comes back into frame, and nothing slides. The feet are still behind the caption band and cannot be rescued — they sit at y~0.97 of the plate, so no window that keeps the avatar this size clears them. "Body included" is a claim about a full-length framing against the busts everywhere else in the film, which this now supports; it is not a claim about toes.
shots._captureNote: The film's only wide shot, and the only frame in which the avatar has legs. That is not a camera trick in the edit — Scene3D's ENVIRONMENT_LOOK parks the camera at 2.4 m landscape / 3.6 m portrait for `datacenter-1970s`, against 0.5 m for the studio, so every other shot is a bust and no `before` step can widen them (capture.config.mjs hazard 9). Collapsing both panels is what makes it work at 9:16: with the Chat Log rail up, the portrait crop of this room keeps the bust and loses the desk entirely. Establishes onboarding itself — same reason as datacenter-diorama.

scenes.caption: No account. No backend required. The cloud is opt-in.
scenes.narration: Five ways to connect a model, a clip library of forty-seven, and a voice that needs no backend at all. None of it needs an account.
scenes._editNote:
'Backend required: none' comes from main — #157 made the browser voice the default, which is what finally made that chip true, and #154 had explicitly left it as a promise to redeem. Carried forward here rather than re-litigated.

One deliberate divergence from main's wording: main's chip reads 'Body clips 47' and this one reads 'Clip LIBRARY 47'. Verified in animationClips.ts, the 47 is 6 VRMA + 34 GLB + 7 feminine across the whole catalog, and NO SINGLE AVATAR LOADS ALL OF THEM — a VRM rig resolves 6, a GLB rig 34. 'Body clips' next to one avatar reads as what that avatar can do, which is false by a factor of about eight. 'Library' is the same number and a true sentence.

The narration says 'a voice that needs no backend at all' rather than 'falls back to the browser' — after #157 the browser voice is the DEFAULT, not a fallback, and describing the default as a fallback undersells it and is wrong.

_honestyNote:
WHAT THIS FILM CLAIMS, AND WHAT HAD TO BE TRUE FIRST.

1. THE VOICE — SETTLED ON MAIN, NOT HERE. The previous cut opened on 'An AI with a face, a voice and a body' while a stock install was mute: ttsConfig defaulted `mode` to 'pocket' at localhost:8000, a server this repo does not ship or start. This branch originally carried its own fix (fall back to speechSynthesis when the backend is unreachable). #157 then landed on main with a better one — it moves the DEFAULT to 'browser' and routes generation and playback through a single effectiveMode() so the two can never disagree — and this branch now takes main's implementation wholesale. The claim is true of every install, so the title card carries it again.

2. THE COUNTS. Verified in animationClips.ts: 6 VRMA + 34 GLB + 7 feminine = 47 clips, and 5 providers in SettingsPanel. But NO SINGLE AVATAR LOADS ALL 47 — a VRM gets 6, a GLB rig 34 — so the chip says 'Clip library' and the narration says 'library'. It must never be phrased as what the avatar on screen can do. EnvironmentPreset is 'none' | 'datacenter-1970s': one optional room plus the plain studio, filmed and worded as one room.

3. THE A-POSE IS A CAPTURE ARTEFACT, AND NOT THE ONE ANYONE EXPECTED. Measured on ANGLE/Metal, asserted from the page: the rig IS live (7 distinct canvas frames across 24s, 46-58 fps). At deviceScaleFactor 1 the avatar leaves bind pose and is in a natural arms-down idle from about 4s. At the capture's dsf 3 the arms stop at 35-40 degrees and do NOT come down at 6s, 12s, 20s, 30s or 45s — same build, same browser, only the scale factor differs. So a USER does not see it and every committed plate does. Root cause not found; recorded in capture.config.mjs hazard 12b rather than guessed at, and left visible in the film rather than cropped around. The cut claims a body.

4. PROP_NEEDS_REEXPORT is untouched. It excludes props whose GLB does not contain the machine its filename claims. The restage on this branch also found WHY four other props render flat — the .blend-sourced ones lost every texture in a lossy re-export — which is written up in docs/DIORAMA.md and needs a Sketchfab login to fix.

5. THE SHOTS ARE PINNED NOW, and an earlier revision of this note said the opposite. It claimed these shots could not be byte-stable because the avatar is a live render loop, and measured 9/18 differing between two identical runs to prove it. #155 then landed on main and did the thing that note had ruled out: it stops the scene rather than tolerating or masking it, via window.__CI_CAPTURE_MODE__ (see services/capture/captureMode.ts), pinning the blink schedule, the diorama's indicator lamps and the pose. That machinery is merged in here, and the lamp pin was re-derived for this branch's lower lamp levels rather than copied — see the merge note in DatacenterDiorama.tsx.

master._orderNote:
THE OPENING WAS AUTHORED IN #156, NARRATED, AND THEN LEFT OUT OF THE FILM.

#165 introduced this `master` array and selected seven beats out of twelve. It dropped the whole three-move opening — the pain, the price, the title — and started the film on `one-turn`, a chat screenshot, under a voice-over promising "voice, expression, and motion". An embodied-AI film has exactly one emotional hook, which is the face, and the cut spent its first eleven seconds on a chat log and a permission modal before showing one.

The library scenes were never touched by #165 and are still the good copy, so this is a restore rather than a rewrite: every line below is the text `scenes[]` already carries, and every mp3 for the four restored cards is the one #156/#160 recorded. Only `already-there` needed a line changed, and its note says why.

The argument now runs: you have talked to it for a year and never seen it -> a face normally costs a game engine and a rig -> Spatial Companion -> here is the face.

master.narration: No account, no sign-in, nothing in the log. There is just something on the other side of the screen, already awake.
master._orderNote:
THE PAYOFF OF THE TITLE CARD, AND THE ONLY LINE IN THIS PASS THAT IS NOT THE LIBRARY'S OWN.

The library line reads "PAST THE MODAL there is no account, no sign-in and nothing in the log. There is just something on the other side of IT, already awake." Both halves are anchored to `first-run`, which used to run before this scene. Here it runs after — the face has to arrive on the title card, not four seconds later behind a blurred permission dialog — so the opening clause became a forward reference to a modal nobody has seen yet, and the "it" it hangs on had no antecedent. Substance, cadence and the best clause are kept verbatim; "of it" becomes "of the screen", which is what the pronoun was doing anyway.

TRANSITION OVERRIDE, AND IT IS THE RULE `your-model` WROTE DOWN. The library scene cuts, because it used to follow `first-run` and a cross-dissolve between two shots of the same app shell is a double-exposure ghost. It now follows `title` — a static intro card that holds for about a second after its two-second read — and a cut would leave that hold uncovered. `your-model`'s `_transitionNote` names this exact boundary as one of the two that must stay dissolving. So: dissolve in, and the name of the product fades into the face it is naming.

MOVED FROM BEAT 2 TO BEAT 5, BEHIND THE FACE.

The plate is a small dialog over a heavily blurred avatar: the darkest, lowest-information frame in the repo, and #165 ran it second, immediately after a promise of voice and expression. It is a real FTUE beat and stays in the film, but it cannot be the film's first look at the product.

Its library caption and narration also come back, because #165's overrides were wrong about their own frame — "Choose how your Companion connects before the first conversation" over a dialog that reads "Enable Microphone / For voice interaction, we need permission to access your microphone. You can skip and use text chat instead." The line is what made a reviewer of the rendered cut describe this beat as a connection-settings screen.

Running it after `already-there` is a one-step step back in time, and the line flags it: "on the first load". `cut`, not the library's dissolve — this and `already-there` are the same app shell with and without a modal over it, which is precisely the pair that ghosts.

Restored before `close`. The tally is the film's only statement of what the thing costs and what it does not ask for, and #165 dropped it, so the cut went from a diorama straight to a sign-off with the ownership argument never made. Its chips and its read are the library's, unchanged: Monthly fee $0, Backend required none, Clip library 47, Model providers 5. It dissolves in from `a-room` and `close` cuts out of it, both as authored.
